newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - loses 3/8 after data, lists.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - loses 3/8 after data, lists.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds lost at least 3/8 point on the day, as prices never recovered from a much stronger-than-expected durable goods report and a heavy offering of bid-wanted lists.

The February durable goods report was expected to show orders fell 0.4 percent, according to a poll of economists by Reuters. Instead, orders rose 1.5 percent, versus an upwardly revised 4.1 percent increase in January.
Analysts said the increases could mean the Federal Reserve, which on Tuesday raised the key federal funds rate by 25 basis points, may need to tighten further.

Adding to the price pressure were heavy slates of bid-wanted lists, traders said. One market analysts said the lists totalled at least $500 million, but traders said many of the bonds seemed to find buyers.
The government long bond, meanwhile, was down 8/32 at 95-15/32 to yield 6.99 percent.
Smith Barney Inc. repriced the day's largest negotiated offering, Hawaii's sale of $584 million of general obligation bonds. The firm raised the yield in 2017 to 5.77 percent from 5.75 percent.

BancAmerica Securities won the day's largest competitive offering, a $45 million Oakland, Calif., general obligation deal. The firm reoffered 2018 bonds at 5.75 percent and did not formally reoffer the 2022 term bonds.
In the secondary market, Jefferson County, Ala., FGIC 5-3/4s of 2027 were 1/4 lower at 97-1/2.

Futures also ended lower. The June municipal contract fell six ticks to 112-27/32, while June Treasury bonds slipped eight ticks to 108-15/32. The MOB spread widened to 140 ticks from 138 at the close on Tuesday.
For the day, municipal bond sales were expected to total $1.1 billion in 30 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
On the competitive side, 11 sales totaling $164 million are on the schedule, with a $45 million Oakland, Calif., deal at 1300 EST the largest.
Thursday's deals total just $6.2 million in two competitive sales ahead of the early close at 1400 EST.
